lesson_title: A Taxi Ride Across the City
hook_text: One taxi ride, city centre to the veld — and you'll pass through every zone in the geography syllabus.
clip_script: Downtown, where you board, the towers are tallest and the pavements fullest — banks, head offices and flagship stores stacked on the priciest ground in the city. Why stack? Because land here is a tug-of-war: every business wants the spot all the taxis and trains converge on, so the ground costs a fortune, and the only way to pay a fortune for a floor is to pile thirty more floors of rent above it. Pull away from the centre and the city turns scruffy and fascinating: old houses split into flats, one building coming down as its neighbour is renovated. Further out the houses begin, then the factory belts along the railways — and just before the city thins into veld, one last stop: an enormous mall ringed by office towers.
visual_style: Continuous side-window taxi shot in fast motion: glass towers sliding into old subdivided houses, then suburbs, then factory fences, ending at a glowing mall at dusk, zone names stamping on screen at each change.
pacing: One continuous accelerating ride with five clear beat-stops, hard brake at the mall.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to name every zone from a single sentence of description.
